M01_relation_name_and_schema.DECISION: public.selected_organization_sessions - an ordinary TABLE (relkind 'r') in schema public.
M01_relation_name_and_schema.schema_rationale_is_the_load_bearing_hal: Schema public is chosen DELIBERATELY AND AT A COST. The stella_0021 closed-world sweep is scoped WHERE n.nspname = 'public' (measured at :393 and :411). A mirror placed in any other schema would be INVISIBLE to it: it would hold organization_id, narrow a storage authorization decision, and carry NO ACL class and NO guard - reproducing exactly the defect stella_0021 exists to prevent, whose own header records that twenty tables reached that state before anybody counted them. Placing the relation in public is choosing to be governed, and the ACL successor act SECTION_4 requires is the price of that choice, not an obstacle to it.
M01_relation_name_and_schema.why_a_table_and_not_a_view_or_unlogged_r: A VIEW cannot hold state. An UNLOGGED table would lose its rows on crash recovery, which is a silent, unobservable widening-to-deny rather than a governed reset, and the second stella_0021 sweep aborts on any relkind outside ('r','p','i','I','c','t') anyway, so a non-table relation in public is refused by the package.
M01_relation_name_and_schema.naming_rationale: Plural snake_case, matching the measured corpus convention (organization_members, account_legal_acceptances, entitlement_grants, legal_instrument_versions). The name says what a ROW IS - a session that has a selected organization - rather than what it is FOR. A name like selected_organizations would read as a durable user preference and would invite exactly the reuse SESSION_SCOPE_RECONCILIATION.prohibited_uses_that_remain_prohibited forbids.
M01_relation_name_and_schema.challenge: The mission packet's candidate did not name the relation. Derived here from the corpus convention.

M02_columns_and_types.DECISION: user_id uuid NOT NULL; session_id uuid NOT NULL; organization_id uuid NOT NULL; selected_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(); expires_at timestamptz NOT NULL. FIVE columns, no more.
M02_columns_and_types.session_id_is_uuid_not_text: MEASURED: auth.sessions.id is uuid (db/baseline/stella_g2_schema.sql:3574). The JWT claim arrives as a JSON string, so the helper casts it. Typing the column uuid makes a malformed claim fail the CAST rather than silently match nothing - the difference between a diagnosable error and an invisible deny. The helper must perform that cast inside its existing EXCEPTION WHEN OTHERS arm, which is why F-S4S-1 requires the denial cause to be discriminated by the probes.
M02_columns_and_types.timestamptz_not_timestamp: Corpus convention and correctness: expiry compared against now() across a deployment whose database and application need not share a zone. MEASURED: auth.sessions mixes both (not_after is timestamptz, refreshed_at is timestamp without time zone); the governed public corpus uses timestamptz, and the governed convention controls here.
M02_columns_and_types.NO_payload_and_NO_free_text: No JSON column, no note, no user agent, no IP. The relation answers exactly one question and carrying anything else would make it a session store, which SESSION_SCOPE_RECONCILIATION forbids. Precedent: stella_0014's operation_tickets is described in its own verification notice as having 'no payload column'.
M02_columns_and_types.challenge: The candidate shape proposed exactly these five columns. CONFIRMED against the corpus, with the uuid and timestamptz choices derived rather than inherited.

M03_primary_key_and_uniqueness.DECISION: PRIMARY KEY (session_id). NO composite primary key and NO separate UNIQUE constraint.
M03_primary_key_and_uniqueness.challenge: THE CANDIDATE SHAPE IS CORRECTED HERE. The mission packet offered 'possible PK(user_id, session_id)' with 'possible UNIQUE(session_id)'. Both together are accepted as a pair only if session_id is NOT globally unique. It IS globally unique - MEASURED: auth.sessions_pkey is PRIMARY KEY (id) at db/baseline/stella_g2_schema.sql:5512. Given that, UNIQUE(session_id) already forbids two rows for one session, so the composite PK constrains NOTHING that the UNIQUE does not, while costing a second index and, far worse, IMPLYING that a session may legitimately appear under more than one user. It may not.
M03_primary_key_and_uniqueness.why_single_key_uniqueness_IS_the_securit: At most one selected organization per session is not a tidiness rule; it is what makes 'read the mirror live' well defined. If two rows could exist for one session, the helper's EXISTS would be satisfied by EITHER, and RAT-STG-01-C2's live read would be a live read of a non-deterministic value. A key that admits the ambiguity cannot be repaired by the read path.
M03_primary_key_and_uniqueness.user_id_remains_NOT_NULL_and_is_CONJOINE: user_id is not part of the key but IS part of the helper predicate: the helper requires session_id = <claim> AND user_id = <auth.uid()>. That conjunct is defence in depth against a WRITER defect - a governed writer that recorded a row under the wrong subject produces a row that matches no caller and therefore grants nothing, instead of narrowing some other subject's storage access. SECTION_7 requires a control proving the conjunct is not vacuous.

M04_is_session_id_globally_unique.DECISION: YES. Globally unique across all users, by measurement, and the design depends on it.
M04_is_session_id_globally_unique.evidence: db/baseline/stella_g2_schema.sql:5508-5512 - CONSTRAINT sessions_pkey PRIMARY KEY (id) on auth.sessions, whose id is uuid NOT NULL (:3574-3575). auth.refresh_tokens.session_id and auth.mfa_amr_claims.session_id are both FKs onto that single-column primary key (:7522, :7586).
M04_is_session_id_globally_unique.what_the_design_takes_from_it: M03's single-column key is sound only because of this. It also means a session_id is meaningless without its owning user: the anti-spoofing conjunct in M11 is checking a pairing that GoTrue already guarantees, so a mismatch is evidence of a defect on our side rather than of a hostile client.
M04_is_session_id_globally_unique.what_the_design_deliberately_does_NOT_ta: Global uniqueness does NOT license an FK. See M05.

M05_foreign_key_topology.DECISION: TWO foreign keys, both into the governed public corpus: user_id REFERENCES public.users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, and organization_id REFERENCES public.organizations(id) ON DELETE CASCADE. NO foreign key to auth.sessions, and none to any relation in schema auth.
M05_foreign_key_topology.NO_auth_FK_is_MEASURED_not_assumed: A sweep of db/migrations/** and db/prepared/** for 'REFERENCES auth.' returns ZERO occurrences across the entire governed corpus. The repository holds schema auth at arm's length on purpose: stella_0013 and stella_0014 each assert that USAGE on schema auth 'exists so that auth.uid() resolves, not to expose the identity store' and each RAISE EXCEPTION if their capability role can read auth.users. db/migrations/0033:53 records that no DB trigger syncs auth.users to public.users. An FK into auth.sessions would be the first of its kind and would invert a posture three packages actively verify.
M05_foreign_key_topology.three_further_reasons_the_auth_FK_is_ref: (a) PRIVILEGE - auth.sessions is OWNED BY supabase_auth_admin; creating an FK onto it requires REFERENCES on that table, which the governed owner does not hold and which is not ours to grant on a managed project. (b) SUBSTRATE - the governed migration chain must apply on a disposable PostgreSQL cluster with no GoTrue; an FK onto auth.sessions would make db/migrations/** unappliable wherever that schema is absent, which is the substrate every Real-PG gate in this repository uses. (c) DRIFT - auth.sessions is a managed, moving target; the baseline already shows it carrying oauth_client_id, refresh_token_hmac_key, refresh_token_counter and scopes, columns added by GoTrue upgrades nobody here controls.
M05_foreign_key_topology.the_cascade_is_an_EXPLICIT_DEVIATION_and: MEASURED: 'ON DELETE CASCADE' appears ZERO times in db/migrations/**. All 68 FKs to public.users and all 41 to public.organizations are written ON DELETE no action ON UPDATE no action. This decision DEVIATES from a one-hundred-percent consistent convention and says so rather than hiding it.
M05_foreign_key_topology.why_the_deviation_is_justified_rather_th: The convention's rationale is preservation: every existing FK protects DURABLE business or audit data, where silently deleting dependent rows would destroy history. The mirror is the repository's FIRST TRANSIENT ENFORCEMENT relation, where preserving history is not merely unnecessary but is the thing SESSION_SCOPE forbids. Under NO ACTION, a stale enforcement row would BLOCK deletion of a user or an organization - an unrelated governed path failing because a storage artifact outlived its session. The convention's reason does not transfer, so the convention does not either.
M05_foreign_key_topology.SECURITY_DOES_NOT_DEPEND_ON_THE_CASCADE: Stated so that a certifier can bound the deviation's blast radius. Because the mirror only NARROWS and membership is a separate live conjunct (RAT-STG-01-C3), an orphan row whose organization was deleted narrows toward an organization in which no active membership can exist, so the helper REFUSES. An orphan is a hygiene defect, never an authorization defect. The cascade is therefore chosen for operational correctness, and the fail-closed property does not rest on it. F-S4S-4 records that a certifier may reasonably prefer NO ACTION, and names what would have to change if the owner or the certifier so decides.

M06_expiry_representation_and_enforcemen.DECISION: expires_at timestamptz NOT NULL, written by the governed writer as now() plus a bounded horizon, and ENFORCED AS PART OF THE HELPER'S LIVENESS PREDICATE - the helper requires expires_at > now(). Enforcement is by predicate FIRST; cleanup (M07) is hygiene only and correctness never depends on it.
M06_expiry_representation_and_enforcemen.this_is_a_MEASURED_repository_precedent_: db/prepared/hosted/stella_0014_operation_tickets.hosted.sql solved the identical problem. Its :122 describes a ticket ceasing to count 'the moment it expires, with NO reaper involved'; its :1384 COMMENT states the hygiene function is 'hygiene only' and that 'The guarantee that an orphaned reservation stops consuming quota does NOT depend on this being called - expires_at is part of the liveness predicate itself.' S4s adopts that structure verbatim in shape.
M06_expiry_representation_and_enforcemen.why_predicate_enforcement_is_strictly_st: A design where expiry is enforced only by deletion is a design where a cleanup outage silently EXTENDS authorization. Under predicate enforcement an expired row is already dead to every reader at the instant it expires, and a cleanup outage costs disk, never reach. That is the difference between a fail-closed and a fail-open expiry, and it is why RAT-STG-01-C8 is satisfied here by the predicate and not by the schedule.
M06_expiry_representation_and_enforcemen.the_horizon: Bounded by the access-token lifetime, MEASURED at supabase/config.toml:186 jwt_expiry = 3600 seconds. The horizon MUST NOT exceed it: a mirror row outliving every token that could present its session_id is unreachable state, and a horizon longer than the token is an expiry that never binds. The exact interval is an implementation constant the implementing lane sets at or below 3600 seconds and pins in a test; this artifact freezes the CEILING and the rule, and deliberately does not invent a number below it.
M06_expiry_representation_and_enforcemen.challenge: The candidate shape proposed expires_at without saying how it is enforced. The enforcement half - predicate first, cleanup never load-bearing - is the substance of this decision and is derived from stella_0014.

M07_cleanup_mechanism.DECISION: OPPORTUNISTIC HYGIENE, performed by the governed writers on the paths that already write. NO scheduler, NO pg_cron, NO background worker, NO external cron. Nothing in the security argument may depend on cleanup having run.
M07_cleanup_mechanism.pg_cron_is_refused_by_MEASUREMENT: db/prepared/hosted/stella_0014_operation_tickets.hosted.sql:1276 states 'THERE IS NO pg_cron IN THIS PROJECT, and this function does not pretend' - an assertion an installed package makes about the project, twice (see also :122). extensions.grant_pg_cron_access() appears in the baseline (db/baseline/stella_g2_schema.sql:507-519) only because the Supabase image ships it as an event trigger. Introducing a scheduler at S4s would contradict a standing, package-level assertion and would add an unowned runtime actor to a node whose whole purpose is to narrow authorization.
M07_cleanup_mechanism.what_proves_it_ran: NOTHING NEEDS TO, and that is the point of M06. The DAG amendment's delegated item asks for 'cleanup - schedule, owner, and what proves it ran'; the honest discharge is that this design REMOVES the obligation rather than satisfying it, because an unproven cleanup cannot extend anybody's reach. What IS proven instead, and is required by SECTION_7, is the stronger property: that an EXPIRED-BUT-PRESENT row is refused. A control asserting 'the row was deleted' would be weaker than a control asserting 'the row, still present and expired, grants nothing'.
M07_cleanup_mechanism.bounded_growth_is_still_required: RAT-STG-01-C8 forbids an unbounded-growth mirror. Growth is bounded by construction: at most one row per live session by M03, deleted on clear and on sign-out by M09/M10, cascaded away with its user or organization by M05, and swept opportunistically by the writers. The bound is structural, not scheduled.

M08_exact_select_writer.DECISION: app/(authenticated)/app/organizations/select/actions.ts, inside the existing selectOrganizationAction, AFTER the isSelectableMember refusal at :103-118 and BEFORE the existing setSelectedOrganization(requestedOrganizationId) at :119. The write is an UPSERT keyed on session_id (see M16).
M08_exact_select_writer.why_this_exact_position: The membership check at :101-118 is deliberately independent of any prior selection - its own comment records that a caller therefore 'has no way to bootstrap a wrong write from a stale carrier'. Writing the mirror BEFORE that check would persist a server-blessed row for an organization the subject may not belong to, which is precisely the authenticity-mistaken-for-authorization failure RAT-STG-01-C3 and probe PG-S4s-4 exist to catch. Writing it BEFORE the cookie keeps the enforcement state at least as narrow as the carrier at every instant: a failure between the two leaves a mirror row with no carrier, which denies, rather than a carrier with no mirror row, which under M12 also denies but by a path that reads as an outage.
M08_exact_select_writer.ordering_rule_frozen: mirror write, THEN carrier write. Never the reverse.
M08_exact_select_writer.the_membership_check_is_NOT_the_authoriz: Stated explicitly so the implementing lane does not treat it as such. This check is a product-level refusal that keeps bad rows out of the table. It is NOT the authorization for the storage operation, which is re-established LIVE inside the helper on every operation by the membership conjunct (M12). A future edit that removed this check would degrade diagnosis and hygiene; it would NOT open cross-organization storage access, because the helper never trusts the row.

M09_exact_clear_writer.DECISION: TWO clear sites, both DELETE of the row for the current session. (a) app/(authenticated)/app/organizations/select/actions.ts clearOrganizationSelectionAction at :128-131, alongside the existing clearSelectedOrganization(). (b) lib/auth/session.ts:297, on the R3 stale/non-member-carrier branch that already calls clearSelectedOrganization().
M09_exact_clear_writer.why_site_b_is_mandatory_and_is_easy_to_m: lib/auth/session.ts:294-299 handles TENANCY_SELECTED_ORGANIZATION_NOT_A_MEMBER by clearing the carrier and redirecting to the selector. If the mirror were left behind on that branch, the repository would hold a server-written row naming an organization the subject has just been measured NOT to be a member of. The helper would still refuse it - membership is a live conjunct - but the row would be exactly the artifact PG-S4s-4 is designed to find, sitting in production as normal operation. Clearing it there keeps the mirror's own content honest rather than relying on the conjunct to compensate.
M09_exact_clear_writer.a_LIVE_GUARD_constrains_how_site_b_is_wr: tests/auth/route-authorization-boundary.test.ts:593-595 asserts that lib/auth/session.ts source contains NO setSelectedOrganization. A mirror CLEAR at :297 does not violate it. A mirror WRITE at that site would have to be refused on the same principle, and the implementing lane must not add one.

M10_exact_signout_writer.DECISION: app/auth/signout/route.ts, a DELETE of the row for the current session, issued STRICTLY BEFORE await supabase.auth.signOut().
M10_exact_signout_writer.the_ordering_is_the_whole_decision: MEASURED: the route today is createClient(); await supabase.auth.signOut(); redirect. After signOut the server no longer holds a verified session from which session_id can be derived, so a delete attempted afterwards has no key to delete BY. The row would survive until expiry with no governed path left to remove it. Delete first, then sign out.
M10_exact_signout_writer.the_residual_window_is_stated_not_hidden: A Supabase sign-out revokes the session server-side, but an already-issued access token remains cryptographically valid until its exp - MEASURED as up to 3600 seconds (supabase/config.toml:186). A holder of that token could still present a valid session_id after sign-out. Deleting the row BEFORE signOut closes the window from our side: the mirror is gone, so M12's fail-closed rule refuses every storage operation for that session regardless of the token's remaining life. This is the concrete reason RAT-STG-01-C1 names sign-out at all, and PG-S4s-5 is the probe that proves it.
M10_exact_signout_writer.this_route_is_a_NEW_write_surface: Recorded plainly because it changes the route's character: app/auth/signout/route.ts performs no database work today. S4s gives it its first. SECTION_5 lists it as ORDINARY, and SECTION_7 requires a control proving the delete precedes the sign-out rather than merely accompanying it.

M11_anti_spoofing_derivation.DECISION: TWO derivations, one per side, and neither ever accepts a client-supplied value. SERVER SIDE: the governed writers derive session_id from the VERIFIED claims of the request's access token via the Supabase auth client's getClaims(), never from a request body, query parameter, header, cookie or form field. HELPER SIDE: the helper derives session_id on the EVALUATING connection from nullif(current_setting('request.jwt.claims', true), '')::jsonb ->> 'session_id', cast to uuid.
M11_anti_spoofing_derivation.why_getClaims_and_not_getUser: MEASURED at the pinned version. @supabase/auth-js 2.108.2 declares getClaims(jwt?, options?) (GoTrueClient.d.ts:2492), while the User interface (types.d.ts:349+) carries NO session_id field - so getUser() CANNOT return it. An implementation reaching for getUser() would find nothing and would be tempted to take the value from somewhere untrusted. Naming the correct call here forecloses that.
M11_anti_spoofing_derivation.what_makes_the_helper_side_UNFORGEABLE_o: The claims GUC is published by the Storage API from a JWT it has already verified, on the very connection that evaluates the policy. A client cannot set a GUC on that connection - it never holds it. Forging session_id therefore requires forging the token signature, which is the same bar that already protects sub, and therefore the same bar that already protects every existing membership decision in this schema. The mechanism adds no new trust assumption; it reuses the one the product already depends on.
M11_anti_spoofing_derivation.the_SAME_GUC_that_auth_uid_already_reads: Deliberate and load-bearing. auth.uid() reads sub from request.jwt.claims (db/baseline/stella_g2_schema.sql:487-494). Reading session_id from the same object means the subject identity and the session identity arrive by ONE transport with ONE verification. A design taking them from two places could be made to disagree; this one cannot.
M11_anti_spoofing_derivation.cross_user_spoofing_is_refused_by_the_co: Even granting a forged session_id for the sake of argument, the helper additionally requires user_id = auth.uid() (M03). An attacker would have to forge BOTH claims in one signed token, at which point the compromise is total and predates S4s. SECTION_7 requires this to be probed rather than argued.

M12_helper_read_path.DECISION: Both helpers gain ONE additional conjunct, read LIVE on every invocation, inline in the body. No new callable, no cached value, no connection-start capture. The conjunct requires that a row exist in public.selected_organization_sessions whose session_id equals the claim, whose user_id equals the passed user_id, whose expires_at > now(), and whose organization_id equals the organization that owns the path's project.
M12_helper_read_path.the_mirror_NARROWS_and_the_membership_co: The existing EXISTS over public.projects joined to public.organization_members - including the write helper's om.role IN ('organization_admin','analyst') and om.status = 'active' - is preserved EXACTLY. The mirror conjunct is ANDed to it, never substituted for any part of it. This is RAT-STG-01-C3 expressed as code shape: a mirror row naming an organization in which the subject is not an active member fails the membership conjunct and REFUSES.
M12_helper_read_path.FAIL_CLOSED_ON_ABSENCE_is_explicit: No row, an expired row, an unparseable claim, or an absent claim ALL deny. There is NO fallback to membership-alone. This is the single most important prohibition in this section: a fallback would re-create defect SI-2 on the storage transport and would make the entire node decorative, since the pre-S4s behaviour IS membership-alone. PG-S4s-5 is the probe that catches it.
M12_helper_read_path.live_per_operation: The read is inside the function body, so it is re-executed on every policy evaluation - which is once per object per operation. Nothing is captured at connection start, and a value that changes mid-connection is observed to change. That is RAT-STG-01-C2 discharged by construction, and PG-S4s-2 is the probe that proves the read is live rather than captured.
M12_helper_read_path.the_existence_guard_must_be_extended: The helpers' opening to_regclass guard covers public.projects and public.organization_members. It MUST be extended to public.selected_organization_sessions, so that a substrate lacking the mirror denies by the SAME diagnosable path as a substrate lacking projects, rather than by an unhandled exception swallowed into the EXCEPTION WHEN OTHERS arm.

M13_helper_body_and_signature_changes.DECISION: BODIES CHANGE. SIGNATURES DO NOT. Both helpers are republished IN PLACE as public.can_read_evidence_object(object_name text, user_id uuid) and public.can_write_evidence_object(object_name text, user_id uuid), preserving argument names, argument types, return type, LANGUAGE plpgsql, SECURITY DEFINER, SET search_path TO '' and OWNER uellix_owner.
M13_helper_body_and_signature_changes.THE_SIGNATURE_PROHIBITION_IS_MECHANICAL_: MEASURED at db/prepared/stella_0021_current_schema_runtime_acl_contract.sql:1141-1159. The section 12 postcondition asserts that NO runtime role holds EXECUTE on an excluded function, and its VALUES list names the two storage helpers by EXACT SIGNATURE - 'public.can_read_evidence_object(text,uuid)' and 'public.can_write_evidence_object(text,uuid)'. The sweep is guarded by WHERE to_regprocedure(t.sig) IS NOT NULL. If a successor CHANGED either signature - by adding a session_id parameter, for instance - to_regprocedure would return NULL for the frozen literal, the row would be filtered out, and the postcondition would PASS WHILE PROVING NOTHING. The guard does not go red; it goes VACUOUS. A signature change would silently disarm a live, currently-load-bearing ACL postcondition, and would do so in the same commit that claimed to strengthen the storage boundary.
M13_helper_body_and_signature_changes.this_is_also_why_the_session_id_is_read_: The two facts compose into a single forced outcome. L3 measured that the policies pass only (name, auth.uid()) and offer no argument position for a session id; M13 measures that creating one would vacuate stella_0021 section 12. Reading the claim from inside the body is therefore not the most convenient option - it is the ONLY option that leaves every existing guard both armed and honest.
M13_helper_body_and_signature_changes.republish_in_place_is_a_precedent_not_a_: db/prepared/stella_0019_storage_write_roles.sql already republishes can_write_evidence_object in place, and its own verification notice records that owner, ACL, SECURITY DEFINER, search_path and argument names were unchanged and that can_read_evidence_object was left byte-identical. S4s follows that pattern for BOTH helpers.
M13_helper_body_and_signature_changes.what_stella_0019_asserts_that_the_succes: stella_0019's verification (at :657-700) measures the storage.objects policies before and after and ABORTS if they changed, and asserts the insert_evidence and delete_evidence policies still call can_write_evidence_object. The S4s successor package must preserve both properties: it changes function BODIES only, and it must recreate NO policy on storage.objects - which is RAT-STG-01-C7 and the stella_0019 invariant in one.

M14_grant_and_revoke_posture.DECISION: ZERO privileges on public.selected_organization_sessions for EVERY non-owner principal. Explicitly: no privilege to uellix_app, uellix_writer or uellix_auditor; none to authenticated, anon or PUBLIC; none to service_role. The relation is reached by OWNERSHIP alone, and by nothing else.
M14_grant_and_revoke_posture.the_helpers_need_no_GRANT_and_that_is_th: Measured at L4: uellix_owner owns public.projects and public.organization_members, neither is FORCEd, and the helpers reach both by owner exemption. The mirror is owned by the same role under the same conditions, so the SECURITY DEFINER bodies reach it with no grant at all. Every grant that is not issued is a grant that cannot be mis-scoped.
M14_grant_and_revoke_posture.RLS_ENABLE_WITHOUT_FORCE_and_why_both_ha: ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY is required because schema public is exposed by PostgREST (MEASURED: supabase/config.toml:20 schemas = ['public','graphql_public']), so the relation is addressable over HTTP and must deny by default at the row layer as well as at the privilege layer. FORCE is NOT set, because FORCE would bind the OWNER to the policies too, the DEFINER helpers would stop reaching the relation, and every storage operation would deny - silently, through the EXCEPTION WHEN OTHERS arm. Both halves are load-bearing and SECTION_7 requires a mutation proving each is detectable.
M14_grant_and_revoke_posture.defence_in_depth_is_deliberate: Zero privilege alone already refuses anon and authenticated; RLS alone would too. Both are present because they fail independently: a future ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES or a hand grant could restore a privilege, and RLS would still deny.
M14_grant_and_revoke_posture.no_new_callable_so_SECTION_5_of_the_ACL_: See M20. The ACL authority's EXECUTE posture of exactly three granted signatures is preserved verbatim.
M14_grant_and_revoke_posture.service_role_is_refused_at_the_design_le: RAT-STG-01-C4. No writer, no helper and no cleanup path in this design uses service_role or an admin client. There is no code path in the frozen mechanism on which one could be introduced without changing this section.

M15_owner_of_the_mirror_relation.DECISION: OWNER uellix_owner - the same role that owns the two storage helpers, public.projects and public.organization_members.
M15_owner_of_the_mirror_relation.why_it_MUST_be_uellix_owner_specifically: A SECURITY DEFINER function executes as its OWNER. The helpers are owned by uellix_owner (MEASURED at db/baseline/stella_g2_schema.sql:884 and :928). For the inline read of M12 to resolve without any grant, uellix_owner must reach the mirror - which ownership provides. Any other owner would force either a GRANT to uellix_owner, widening the surface M14 exists to keep at zero, or a failure into the EXCEPTION WHEN OTHERS arm.
M15_owner_of_the_mirror_relation.a_RUNTIME_role_may_NOT_own_it_and_the_pa: MEASURED at db/prepared/stella_0021_current_schema_runtime_acl_contract.sql:471-478. Section 0(b) sweeps pg_class for relations in public whose relowner is uellix_writer, uellix_auditor or uellix_app and RAISES 'a runtime role OWNS relation(s) % in schema public. An owner is not constrained by the grants this package issues, so the contract it would certify would not be the contract in force.' uellix_owner is NOT one of the three runtime roles, so this decision satisfies that abort rather than tripping it - checked, not assumed.

M16_cross_organization_switch_behaviour.DECISION: A switch is an ATOMIC REPLACE: a single INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (session_id) DO UPDATE SET organization_id = EXCLUDED.organization_id, selected_at = now(), expires_at = <new horizon>, with a WHERE guard requiring the existing row's user_id to equal the writing subject. One statement, no delete-then-insert.
M16_cross_organization_switch_behaviour.why_not_DELETE_then_INSERT: A two-statement switch has an interval - however short - in which the session has NO row. Under M12 that interval denies every storage operation, so a switch would produce sporadic, unreproducible refusals on an unrelated path. The single-statement upsert has no such interval: the session moves from organization A to organization B with no state in between, and M03's key makes 'no state in between' expressible at all.
M16_cross_organization_switch_behaviour.the_user_id_guard_on_the_UPDATE_arm: Without it, a conflict on session_id would overwrite whatever row was there, including - if a writer defect ever produced one - a row belonging to another subject. With it, such a write affects zero rows and the defect surfaces as a failure rather than as a silent cross-subject overwrite.
M16_cross_organization_switch_behaviour.the_switch_is_visible_on_the_NEXT_operat: This is the property that discharges RAT-STG-01-C5's second half. A claim-based design carries a stale window until the token is reissued; here the organization is not in the token at all, so the next helper evaluation reads the new row. The session_id claim does not change across a switch, which is exactly why it is the right key.

M17_in_flight_operation_behaviour.DECISION: STATED, BOUNDED, AND NOT PAPERED OVER. A storage operation already in flight across the Storage API boundary when a switch occurs is NOT retroactively re-evaluated. Policy evaluation happens once, at the moment the Storage API evaluates the row; an operation whose evaluation completed under organization A completes under organization A.
M17_in_flight_operation_behaviour.why_this_cannot_be_fixed_at_S4s_and_must: The application transaction that performs the switch and the Storage API connection that evaluates the policy are DIFFERENT CONNECTIONS ON DIFFERENT TRANSPORTS - the finding TENANCY_S4_EXECUTION_AUTHORITY_v1.0.0 B1_REDERIVATION established and this lane re-derived at L5. There is no shared transaction in which both could be made atomic. Any design claiming to re-evaluate an in-flight operation would be asserting a coupling that measurably does not exist.
M17_in_flight_operation_behaviour.the_bound_that_makes_it_acceptable: The exposure is one already-authorized operation, for an organization the subject was an active member of at evaluation time, for the duration of that single operation. It is not a window in which NEW operations can be started against the old organization: the very next evaluation reads the new row. Membership remains a live conjunct throughout, so this is never a path to an organization the subject does not belong to.
M17_in_flight_operation_behaviour.recorded_as_an_OPEN_FINDING_rather_than_: F-S4S-2. Resolving it would require the storage write path to hold a transaction across the upload, which lib/pipeline/evidence.ts:316-339 documents as deliberately rejected because holding a pooled connection for a 25 MB upload is unacceptable. S4s does not reopen that decision.

M18_membership_revocation_behaviour.DECISION: MEMBERSHIP REVOCATION DOES NOT WRITE THE MIRROR. No revocation path is added to the write set, and no mirror row is deleted when a membership is revoked or deactivated.
M18_membership_revocation_behaviour.why_that_is_correct_rather_than_an_omiss: This is the single clearest demonstration that RAT-STG-01-C3 is doing real work. Because membership is re-established LIVE inside the helper on every operation, a revoked member's surviving mirror row grants NOTHING the instant the membership row's status leaves 'active' - with no write to the mirror, no cache to invalidate, and no propagation delay. Revocation takes effect at the speed of the next operation.
M18_membership_revocation_behaviour.the_alternative_would_be_STRICTLY_WORSE: A design that deleted mirror rows on revocation would be a design in which revocation DEPENDED on that delete succeeding - introducing a propagation path that can fail, be missed on a new revocation site, or race. It would convert an invariant into a procedure. PG-S4s-4 exists to prove the invariant holds without the procedure.
M18_membership_revocation_behaviour.hygiene_is_still_served: The revoked member's row expires within the M06 horizon and is cascaded away if the user or organization is deleted. No new path is needed.

M19_restore_reset_and_deletion_behaviour.DECISION: RESET ON RESTORE. See SECTION_8 for the full derivation. On any database restore or point-in-time recovery, public.selected_organization_sessions is TRUNCATED as part of bringing the system up, before it serves traffic. Deletion of individual rows is covered by M07/M09/M10 and by the M05 cascades.
M19_restore_reset_and_deletion_behaviour.summary_of_the_reason: The mirror is transient enforcement state derived from a carrier, not durable business data. A restore re-materializes rows for sessions that no longer exist, keyed by session_ids GoTrue may since have reissued, and restores our table and GoTrue's session store to points that need not agree. Truncating costs every live session one re-selection - a product inconvenience already contemplated by SESSION_SCOPE - and removes the entire class of restore-induced mis-narrowing.

M20_whether_a_new_callable_is_required.DECISION: NO NEW CALLABLE. The mirror is read INLINE inside the two existing helper bodies. No function, no view and no procedure is created by S4s.

SECTION_7_REAL_INTEGRATION_TEST_CONTRACT.RULE_1_the_harness_must_reproduce_the_CO: Inherited from the retired PG-2's lesson and restated as binding. A probe that opens one session, sets the claims itself, and calls the helper FABRICATES on one connection exactly the propagation production lacks. Every control below that claims to prove a transport property must use the real transport or at minimum two distinct connections. A single-session harness silently passes a fabricated propagation.
SECTION_7_REAL_INTEGRATION_TEST_CONTRACT.RULE_2_a_DENIAL_must_be_ATTRIBUTED_not_m: This is the discriminator F-S4S-1 forces. Both helpers end in EXCEPTION WHEN OTHERS THEN RETURN false, so a permission error, an absent relation, a malformed claim and an honest policy denial are all observationally false. Every negative control MUST additionally establish that the intended predicate is what refused - by asserting the SETUP succeeded, by showing the positive twin of the same fixture PERMITS, or by discriminating the SQLSTATE where one is reachable. A negative control that asserts only 'false' is vacuous under this helper shape and does not discharge its obligation.

REQUIRED_FALSIFICATIONS.obligation: A server-written, live, unexpired mirror row naming organization A, for a subject with NO active membership in A, REFUSES every evidence-object operation. Discharges RAT-STG-01-C3 and PG-S4s-4. The positive twin - same subject, same row, membership restored - must PERMIT, or the refusal is unattributed.

A dual-member subject with a live mirror row naming A is REFUSED for B across insert, select/download, delete and the erasure path, and PERMITTED for A. SYMMETRY IS MANDATORY: the read surface is measurably broader than the write surface, so a control exercising writes alone understates the exposure. PG-S4s-3.
Subject S1 presenting session X, with a mirror row keyed to session Y of the same subject, is REFUSED. Proves the session_id conjunct is load-bearing and not decorative.

A mirror row whose expires_at is in the past REFUSES while STILL PRESENT in the table. This is the control that proves M06's predicate enforcement rather than M07's cleanup. Deleting the row first would prove the weaker property and must not be substituted.
After a switch from A to B on one session, the NEXT operation is permitted for B and refused for A, with NO token refresh. Proves M16 and the C5 stale-window discharge.

After sign-out, an operation presenting the still-cryptographically-valid pre-sign-out token is REFUSED, because the row is gone. Proves M10's ordering. Requires a real token that outlives the session, so it is REAL-INTEGRATION-ONLY.
With the mirror row untouched, flipping the membership status away from active REFUSES immediately. Proves M18 - that revocation needs no mirror write.

A subject calling the Storage API DIRECTLY with its own anon key and JWT, bypassing every server route, is bound by the same boundary. This is the criterion the whole node exists for: the server already enforces selection today, so a control that only exercises server routes proves nothing S4s adds. REAL-INTEGRATION-ONLY, and the single most important control in this manifest.

With app.organization_id set transaction-locally on connection A, the helper invoked on connection B observes NO value for it. PG-S4s-1. MUST use two distinct connections - a single-session harness cannot express it and would silently pass a fabricated propagation.

With NO row for the session - never written, cleared, or expired - every operation is refused and NONE is silently defaulted to any membership. PG-S4s-5. This is the control that catches a fallback re-creating SI-2 on the storage transport, and it is the control a well-meaning implementation is most likely to break.

A token whose session_id claim is absent or is not a uuid REFUSES, AND the control establishes that the claim is what refused rather than some unrelated failure. SECTION_8_RESTORE_RECOVERY.CLASSIFICATION: RESET_ON_RESTORE. public.selected_organization_sessions is TRUNCATED as part of any database restore or point-in-time recovery, before the restored system serves traffic. It is NOT durable business state and is NOT restored.
SECTION_8_RESTORE_RECOVERY.the_expected_principle_was_RE_DERIVED_no: The mission names RESET_ON_RESTORE as the expected principle and requires the exact rule to be re-derived. The derivation follows, and it does not rest on the expectation.
SECTION_8_RESTORE_RECOVERY.derivation_1_the_frozen_SESSION_SCOPE_do: MULTI_ORG_TENANT_SCOPE_AUTHORITY_v1.0.0 SESSION_SCOPE, as narrowly amended by AM-STG-S5, holds that the selection is not restored across sessions and that the mirror is enforcement state DERIVED FROM the carrier rather than a carrier itself. State derived from a carrier cannot outlive it: restoring the derived state while the carrier is gone inverts the direction of the derivation.
SECTION_8_RESTORE_RECOVERY.derivation_2_the_key_is_meaningless_afte: A row is addressable only by a session_id that GoTrue issued. A restore returns OUR table to one point in time; GoTrue's auth.sessions is a separate store that need not be restored to the same point, and may since have reissued ids. A restored row is therefore keyed by a session that may not exist, or - worse - by an id that now belongs to a DIFFERENT session. There is no restore procedure available to us that makes the two stores agree.
SECTION_8_RESTORE_RECOVERY.derivation_3_the_failure_mode_is_MIS_NAR: Bounded honestly rather than overstated. Because membership remains a live conjunct, a stale row can never grant access to an organization the subject does not belong to. What it CAN do is narrow a session to an organization the subject did not currently select - permitting A when the user had since chosen B. That is a correctness and least-surprise defect, not a tenancy breach. The classification does not depend on inflating it.
SECTION_8_RESTORE_RECOVERY.derivation_4_the_cost_of_resetting_is_al: Truncation costs every live session one re-selection. SESSION_SCOPE already holds that a session begins with NO selection and that the selector is the normal entry point, and NO_AUTO_SELECTION already forbids inferring one. So the post-restore state - every session unselected, every subject routed to the selector - is a state the product already implements and already handles. Resetting costs nothing that is not already a supported path.
SECTION_8_RESTORE_RECOVERY.derivation_5_fail_closed_is_the_tie_brea: Per CLAUDE.md section 5, where the correct state is unknown the posture is preserve-or-stop, never guess. An empty mirror DENIES until a governed writer re-populates it. A restored mirror PERMITS on the basis of a selection nobody can confirm was current. Only one of those two is fail-closed, and it is the empty one.
SECTION_8_RESTORE_RECOVERY.the_exact_rule: On restore or PITR, and before the restored system serves traffic, TRUNCATE public.selected_organization_sessions. The truncation is part of the restore procedure, not a background job, and not a consequence of expiry - relying on expiry would leave a window of up to the M06 horizon in which restored rows are live.
SECTION_8_RESTORE_RECOVERY.what_this_does_NOT_authorize: It does not authorize any change to backup, restore or PITR tooling in this act, and it does not create a restore runbook. It states the classification and the rule that a restore procedure must carry, which is the obligation RI-13 proves.

self_check.could_a_control_written_against_this_art: Addressed structurally rather than denied. SECTION_7 RULE_2 exists because the helper's EXCEPTION WHEN OTHERS arm makes bare denial assertions vacuous, and MU-04 exists because the user_id conjunct is redundant under a correct writer and a redundant conjunct that no control distinguishes is a known masking shape in this repository. MU-06 exists because the most likely implementation defect - falling back to membership-alone - reproduces the pre-S4s behaviour exactly, so a suite that stays green under it proves nothing about the node.
self_check.the_temptation_this_lane_had_to_refuse: To author the ACL amendment v1.0.2 here. It would have been ONE more docs-only file, it would have made the node look closed, and the mission explicitly permitted it if governance-valid. It was refused because the measurement did not support it: three of three commits in the ACL lineage are single-domain, the only cross-domain precedent is the allocation pattern this lane is forbidden, and the amendment would have classified a relation shape that step 5 has not yet certified. Bundling it would have converted a certifiable adjudication into an unauthorized act that looked like progress.
self_check.the_second_temptation: To read the session id by adding a parameter to the helpers, which is the obvious design and reads as cleaner. It would have silently vacuated stella_0021 section 12's negative list via its to_regprocedure guard - a live postcondition passing while proving nothing, in the same commit that claimed to strengthen the storage boundary. The measurement at M13 is what caught it.
self_check.counts_are_rederived_not_restated: Every count in this self_check is computed FROM the array it counts at materialization time, never transcribed from prose elsewhere in the artifact. A count restated by hand is covered by no control and is a known defect class in this repository.
